title: Breaking a discount habit
headline: Rebuilt a discount-addicted brand around full-price demand
blurb: Fernwood had trained its customers to wait for a sale. We rewrote the positioning, rebuilt the creative system and moved the media plan off promo.
challenge: Eleven consecutive quarters of discounting had reset customer expectations. Full-price sell-through sat under a fifth of volume, and every attempt to hold price collapsed within a fortnight.
approach: We started by killing the promo calendar for a single category as a controlled test, then rebuilt the brand story around materials and repairability rather than price. Creative moved from product-on-white to in-home documentary. Lifecycle stopped announcing sales and started teaching care and pairing.
outcome: Full-price sell-through more than doubled inside three quarters. Contribution margin rose 61% on flat revenue, and the promo calendar shrank from eleven events a year to three.

title: Pipeline without the founders
headline: Turned a founder-led sales motion into a repeatable pipeline engine
blurb: Two founders were the only source of demand. We built a category narrative, a content engine and a paid programme that filled the calendar without them.
challenge: Every qualified opportunity traced back to one of two founders speaking somewhere. Marketing produced volume but nothing that converted, and nobody agreed on what a lead was worth.
approach: We wrote a category narrative the founders actually believed, turned their conference talks into a durable content engine, and rebuilt the measurement layer so sales and marketing were reading the same pipeline number.
outcome: Qualified pipeline tripled while founder-sourced share fell from 88% to 31%. Cost per SQL dropped 41% even as volume grew.

title: The numbers were the bug
headline: Cut acquisition cost in half by fixing measurement first
blurb: Nothing was broken except the numbers. Server-side tracking and a geo holdout revealed a third of spend was buying customers they already had.
challenge: Platform-reported ROAS looked healthy while blended CAC climbed every month. Nobody could reconcile the two, so budget kept flowing to the channel with the best self-reported numbers.
approach: We rebuilt tracking server-side, rebased attribution in the warehouse, and ran a four-week geo holdout on the largest channel. The holdout showed roughly a third of that spend was reaching people who would have converted anyway.
outcome: Blended CAC fell 48% in two quarters. Freed budget moved to prospecting and a lifecycle programme that had never been funded.

title: Growing the other side
headline: Made supply-side growth the marketing team's problem
blurb: Buyer demand was never the constraint. We built a seller acquisition programme with its own creative, funnel and payback model.
challenge: Buyers arrived faster than inventory could support, so conversion fell and paid spend on the demand side became actively harmful.
approach: We treated sellers as a separate acquisition problem with its own creative territory, onboarding funnel and payback model, then rebuilt the listing flow around the first fifteen minutes.
outcome: Nearly three thousand activated sellers in six months, time-to-first-listing down a third, and buyer-side conversion recovered without extra demand spend.

title: Outrunning the algorithm
headline: A creative testing cadence that outran the algorithm
blurb: Forty concepts a month, read against installs and day-30 retention. Winners got scaled, losers got buried, nobody got precious.
metricLabel: return on ad spend at scale
challenge: Creative fatigue was arriving inside nine days. The in-house team could produce six concepts a month, which meant most of the budget ran on assets everyone already knew were tired.
approach: We built a modular concept system — hooks, proofs and closes that recombine — so forty assets a month came from ten shoots. Every asset carried a hypothesis and was read against day-30 retention, not installs.
outcome: ROAS held at 5.1x while spend tripled. Day-30 retention rose 27% because the winning hooks were selecting for better users, not just cheaper ones.

title: Eleven stores, one brand
headline: Took eleven regional stores into one national brand
blurb: A single identity, a local-first media plan and a lifecycle programme that knew which store you shopped at.
challenge: Eleven stores operating as eleven brands, with local managers buying their own media and no shared customer record.
approach: One identity flexible enough for local voice, a media plan built on store catchments rather than national reach, and a loyalty programme tied to the store you actually shop at.
outcome: Same-store revenue up 34%, loyalty enrolment up 52%, and thirteen new openings that sold out their first weekend before launch day.

title: Proof over promises
headline: Replaced sustainability claims with evidence people could check
blurb: A crowded shelf full of green promises. We made verifiability the brand's entire creative platform.
challenge: Every competitor made the same environmental claims, so none of them registered. Trial was expensive and repeat was flat.
approach: We built the platform around checkable proof — batch-level sourcing on pack, third-party audits published in full, and creative that invited scrutiny instead of asking for trust.
outcome: Retail velocity nearly tripled in target doors, cost per trial fell 24%, and unaided awareness climbed 19 points in the core market.

title: Fewer, better guests
headline: Halved enquiry volume and doubled booked revenue
blurb: The funnel was full of people who would never book. We deliberately made it narrower and much more expensive to enter.
metricLabel: booked revenue on half the leads
challenge: A sales team drowning in enquiries with a 2% booking rate, and a media programme rewarded for producing more of them.
approach: We put price in the creative, qualified hard on the landing page, and rebuilt bidding around booked revenue rather than form fills.
outcome: Enquiries halved, booking rate rose almost fourfold, and booked revenue doubled with the same media budget.
